claim: Murine embryonic stem cells (mESC) were fused with human endothelial cells in stable, non-dividing, heterokaryons.
source: Murine embryonic stem cells (mESC) were fused with human endothelial cells in stable, non-dividing, heterokaryons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and demonstrated through experimental procedures described in the methods and results sections.

claim: Using RNA-seq, it is possible to discriminate between human and mouse transcripts in chimeric heterokaryons.
source: Using RNA-seq, it is possible to discriminate between human and mouse transcripts in these chimeric heterokaryons.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology and demonstrates successful discrimination of species-specific transcripts through RNA-seq analysis.

claim: A temporal pattern of gene expression in the ESCs of the heterokaryons recapitulated ontogeny, with early mesodermal factors being expressed before mature endothelial genes.
source: We observed a temporal pattern of gene expression in the ESCs of the heterokaryons that recapitulated ontogeny, with early mesodermal factors being expressed before mature endothelial genes.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and RNA-seq data showing sequential activation of genes like Kdr (early) followed by Vwf (later).

claim: POU class 3 homeobox 2 (Pou3f2) is a transcriptional factor not previously known to be involved in endothelial development that was upregulated in heterokaryons.
source: A set of transcriptional factors not known to be involved in endothelial development was upregulated, one of which was POU class 3 homeobox 2 (Pou3f2).
evidence: RNA-seq data identified Pou3f2 as an upregulated transcription factor in the heterokaryon system.

claim: Pou3f2 is important in differentiation to endothelial lineage as confirmed via loss- and gain-of-function studies.
source: We confirmed its importance in differentiation to endothelial lineage via loss- and gain-of-function (LOF and GOF).
evidence: The manuscript presents data from shRNA knockdown experiments and rescue experiments with modified mRNA showing effects on endothelial differentiation.

claim: The role of Pou3f2 in vascular development was validated in zebrafish embryos using morpholino oligonucleotides.
source: Its role in vascular development was validated in zebrafish embryos using morpholino oligonucleotides.
evidence: Zebrafish experiments using morpholinos showed reduced intersegmental vessels and impaired vascular development.

claim: Our understanding of the genetic and epigenetic processes governing endothelial development and differentiation is limited.
source: Our understanding of the genetic and epigenetic processes governing endothelial development and differentiation is limited (Yan et al., 2010; De Val and Black, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Methodologies for obtaining endothelial cells from pluripotent stem cells are empirically driven and suboptimal.
source: Accordingly, our methodologies for obtaining endothelial cells from pluripotent stem cells are empirically driven and suboptimal (Choi et al., 2009; James et al., 2010; Huang et al., 2010a, 2010b; Wong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work in the field.

claim: There is unexplained inconsistency in the yield of iPSC-ECs.
source: There is unexplained inconsistency in the yield of iPSC-ECs; in the stability of their phenotype; and in the fidelity of differentiation (in terms of replicating the epigenetic and genetic profile of a mature endothelial cell).
evidence: This is stated as a known problem in the field based on established knowledge.

claim: The ability to efficiently generate specific endothelial subtypes (e.g. arterial, venous, lymphatic) is poor.
source: Furthermore, our ability to efficiently generate specific endothelial subtypes (e.g. arterial, venous, lymphatic) is poor.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the field based on current knowledge.

claim: In 95% of cases, the species-specific nucleotide differences between the mouse and human transcripts permit differentiation between reads of murine versus human transcripts when sequences are aligned to their respective genomes.
source: In 95% of cases, the species-specific nucleotide differences between the mouse and human transcripts would permit us to differentiate between reads of murine versus human transcripts when the sequences were aligned to their respective genomes.
evidence: This is based on the bioinformatic analysis of RNA-seq data from heterokaryons.

claim: Heterokaryons expressed cell surface markers and characteristics of both cell types (mESC and hEC).
source: To discover new genes involved in endothelial specification, we made heterokaryons consisting of human endothelial cells (hEC) and murine embryonic stem cells (mESC) (Figure 1a–c), which expressed cell surface markers and characteristics of both cell types.
evidence: This is demonstrated through FACS analysis and immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 1.

claim: Factors that are actively maintaining endothelial phenotype would act on the pluripotent stem cell nuclei to induce expression of key determinants of endothelial lineage.
source: We hypothesized that the factors that are actively maintaining endothelial phenotype (transcription factors, epigenetic modifiers and non-coding RNA etc) would act on the pluripotent stem cell nuclei to induce expression of key determinants of endothelial lineage.
evidence: This is the hypothesis underlying the experimental approach, supported by subsequent experimental data.

claim: There is no nuclear fusion, chromosome rearrangement, or chromosome loss in the heterokaryons.
source: Since there is no nuclear fusion, chromosome rearrangement, or chromosome loss in the heterokaryons (Bhutani et al., 2010), we reasoned that this synchronization would permit us to study the temporal sequence of reprogramming to endothelial lineage using RNA seq.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work by Bhutani et al., 2010.

claim: Upregulation of murine endothelial genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf was observed in mESCs fused with human endothelial cells.
source: In mESCs which were fused with human endothelial cells, we observed upregulation of murine endothelial genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf (Figure 1d–g)
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1d-g.

claim: Transcription factors involved in endothelial development such as Etv2, Ets1 and Tal1 were upregulated in heterokaryons of mESC with hEC.
source: In mESCs which were fused with human endothelial cells, we observed upregulation of murine endothelial genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf (Figure 1d–g), and transcription factors involved in endothelial development such as Etv2, Ets1 and Tal1 (Figure 1l–n).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1l-n.

claim: The expression of endothelial genes in heterokaryons seemed to mirror ontogeny, with genes involved early in mesoderm specification (e.g. Kdr) expressed earlier than genes more specific to hemato-endothelial lineage (e.g. Von Willebrand factor).
source: Intriguingly, the expression of these genes seemed to mirror ontogeny, in that genes involved early in mesoderm specification (e.g. Kdr) were expressed earlier in the heterokaryon, whereas genes that are more specific to hemato-endothelial lineage (e.g. Von Willebrand factor) were expressed later.
evidence: This is based on temporal qPCR data showing sequential gene activation patterns.

claim: Down-regulation of genes encoding pluripotent factors (Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog) was observed in heterokaryons.
source: In parallel to the upregulation of genes involved in endothelial development, we observed down-regulation of genes encoding pluripotent factors (Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog) (Figure 1o).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1o.

claim: Upregulation of human genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf was observed in hiPSCs fused with murine endothelial cells.
source: We observed in the pluripotent cells an upregulation of human genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf (Figure 1h–k)
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1h-k.

claim: Transcription factors involved in endothelial development such as Etv2, Ets1 and Tal1 were upregulated in heterokaryons of hiPSC with mEC.
source: We observed in the pluripotent cells an upregulation of human genes including Kdr, Tie2, Cdh5 and Vwf (Figure 1h–k), and transcription factors involved in endothelial development such as Etv2, Ets1 and Tal1 (Figure 1p–r).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1p-r.

claim: A temporal sequence that mirrored ontogeny was observed in hiPSC/mEC heterokaryons, with parallel downregulation of genes encoding pluripotent factors (Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog).
source: Again, we observed a temporal sequence that mirrored ontogeny, with a parallel downregulation of genes encoding pluripotent factors (Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog) (Figure 1s).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1s.

claim: The heterokaryon system demonstrates rapid induction of endothelial genes which appears to recapitulate endothelial development.
source: These results demonstrate rapid induction of endothelial genes in the heterokaryon which appears to recapitulate endothelial development.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the temporal gene expression data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Heterokaryons were harvested at 6–24 hr post-fusion based on qPCR data showing rapid sequential activation of endothelial genes as early as 6 hr post-fusion.
source: Heterokaryons were double-positive cells (GFP+ for mESC and CellTracker Red+ for hECs) and were harvested at 6–24 hr post-fusion. These time points were chosen based on our qPCR data, which showed rapid sequential activation of endothelial genes as early as 6 hr post-fusion.
evidence: This is based on preliminary qPCR experiments that informed the experimental design.

claim: The RNAseq analysis of the heterokaryon samples (mESC/hEC) revealed a set of 1297 genes in the mESC that were upregulated.
source: The RNAseq analysis of the heterokaryon samples (mESC/hEC) revealed a set of 1297 genes in the mESC that were upregulated as well as a set of 795 genes that were downregulated after fusion with hEC (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The RNAseq analysis of the heterokaryon samples (mESC/hEC) revealed a set of 795 genes in the mESC that were downregulated after fusion with hEC.
source: The RNAseq analysis of the heterokaryon samples (mESC/hEC) revealed a set of 1297 genes in the mESC that were upregulated as well as a set of 795 genes that were downregulated after fusion with hEC (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The upregulated genes in heterokaryons included known endothelial related genes, for example, Kdr and Vwf, as well as hemangioblast markers, that is, angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, CD143).
source: The upregulated genes included known endothelial related genes, for example, Kdr and Vwf, as well as hemangioblast markers, that is, angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, CD143).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data analysis identifying specific upregulated genes.

claim: Murine pluripotency markers were down-regulated in heterokaryons.
source: Conversely, murine pluripotency markers were down-regulated.
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Novel transcriptional factors such as Tbx1, Cebpd, Nrarp, Pou3f2, Maf, Tbx20, Tigd5, Pdn and Batf2 were identified in the RNA-seq analysis.
source: We identified some novel transcriptional factors (such as Tbx1, Cebpd, Nrarp, Pou3f2, Maf, Tbx20, Tigd5, Pdn and Batf2), and targeted one of these (Pou3f2) for further study.
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data analysis identifying upregulated transcription factors.

claim: Unbiased hierarchical clustering analysis indicated that the transcriptome of the mESC in the heterokaryon is closer to that of mESCs differentiated toward EC lineage, than to the parental mESCs.
source: Unbiased hierarchical clustering analysis indicated that the transcriptome of the mESC in the heterokaryon is closer to that of mESCs differentiated toward EC lineage, than to the parental mESCs (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is based on hierarchical clustering analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The transcriptome of mESC co-cultured (but not fused) with hECs bears a closer relationship to the transcriptome of the parental mESCs.
source: By contrast, the transcriptome of mESC co-cultured (but not fused) with hECs bears a closer relationship to the transcriptome of the parental mESCs.
evidence: This is based on hierarchical clustering analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: Differentially up- or down-regulated genes in the mESC in heterokaryons are similar to those in mESC exposed to the endothelial differentiation protocol.
source: Global gene function enrichment analysis indicates that differentially up- or down-regulated genes in the mESC in heterokaryons are similar to those in mESC exposed to the endothelial differentiation protocol (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is based on gene function enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The upregulated genes in the heterokaryons tend to be involved in transcription regulation, RNA alternative splicing, DNA binding, embryonic organ development, differentiation and regulation of cell proliferation.
source: In particular, the upregulated genes in the heterokaryons tend to be involved in transcription regulation, RNA alternative splicing, DNA binding, embryonic organ development, differentiation and regulation of cell proliferation (Figure 2e)
evidence: This is based on functional enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Downregulated genes in heterokaryons are implicated in ATP and ribonucleotide binding.
source: whereas downregulated genes are implicated in ATP and ribonucleotide binding (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is based on functional enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The heterokaryon system may serve as an effective model for cell differentiation.
source: These results suggest that the heterokaryon system may serve as an effective model for cell differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the RNA-seq and functional analysis data.

claim: The expression of Pou3f2 was up-regulated at 6-hr post-fusion and its expression then declined over the ensuing 48 hr in heterokaryons.
source: Accordingly, we examined the temporal sequence of gene expression of Pou3f2 in the heterokaryon system (Figure 3a). The expression of Pou3f2 was up-regulated at 6-hr post-fusion and its expression then declined over the ensuing 48 hr.
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The expression of Pou3f2 increased from Day 3 to Day 7 and then declined in the later phase (11 days) of the endothelial differentiation protocol.
source: Specifically, the expression of Pou3f2 increased from Day 3 to Day 7 and then declined in the later phase (11 days) of the endothelial differentiation protocol.
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data during mESC differentiation to endothelial cells.

claim: The regulation of mesodermal and EC genes was accelerated when ESCs were placed into heterokaryons versus the standard endothelial differentiation protocol.
source: Notably, the expression of other mesodermal and EC genes followed a similar pattern, in that their regulation was accelerated when ESCs were placed into heterokaryons versus the standard endothelial differentiation protocol.
evidence: This is based on comparison of temporal gene expression patterns between heterokaryons and standard differentiation.

claim: Current differentiation protocols could be considerably improved.
source: This observation is consistent with the notion that current differentiation protocols could be considerably improved.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that heterokaryons show accelerated gene regulation compared to standard protocols.

claim: Lentiviral mediated shRNA knockdown of Pou3f2 reduced the gene expressions of endothelial markers including Kdr, Tie2, Nos3, Cdh5 and Vwf at Day 8 following endothelial differentiation from mESC.
source: We found that KD of Pou3f2 reduced the expression of endothelial genes including Kdr, Tie2, Nos3, Cdh5 and Vwf at Day 8 of the differentiation protocol (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Knockdown of Pou3f2 reduced the gene expressions of transcription factors involved in endothelial differentiation such as Ets1, Erg, Etv2 and Fli1 in mESC differentiated to endothelial lineage at Day 8.
source: Similarly, the expression of endothelial transcription factors such as Ets1, Erg, Etv2 and Fli1 were also reduced in the Pou3f2 KD mESC (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The knockdown of Pou3f2 in mESC did not affect the expression of mesoderm- (Bmp4, T), endoderm- (Cxcr4, Gata4) or ectoderm- (Pax6 and Nestin) related genes.
source: The KD of Pou3f2 in mESC did not affect the expression of mesoderm- (Bmp4, T), endoderm- (Cxcr4, Gata4) or ectoderm- (Pax6 and Nestin) related genes (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The generation of mESC-derived CD31+ and CD144+ cells were reduced by over 50% in Pou3f2 knockdown group.
source: Notably, the generation of mESC-derived CD31+ and CD144+ cells were reduced by over 50% in Pou3f2 KD group (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FACS analysis shown in Figure 3f-g.

claim: Pou3f2 knockdown mESC-derived endothelial cells manifested poor network formation on matrigel.
source: Furthermore, Pou3f2 KD mESC-derived endothelial cells manifested poor network formation on matrigel (Figure 3h).
evidence: This is demonstrated through matrigel network formation assay shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Pou3f2 seems to be necessary for the full expression of genes known to be involved in endothelial development, and for the efficient generation of fully functioning endothelial cells.
source: To summarize, Pou3f2 seems to be necessary for the full expression of genes known to be involved in endothelial development, and for the efficient generation of fully functioning endothelial cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the loss-of-function experiments.

claim: The Wnt/B-catenin signalling pathway is highly conserved and regulates vascular cell fate and development through Dll4/Notch signalling.
source: The Wnt/B-catenin signalling pathway is highly conserved and regulates vascular cell fate and development through Dll4/Notch signalling (Corada et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Corada et al., 2010.

claim: The promoter for the Pou3f2 gene is a direct target for β-catenin/Lef1.
source: The promoter for the Pou3f2 gene is a direct target for β-catenin/Lef1 (Goodall et al., 2004a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Goodall et al., 2004a.

claim: The PI3K pathway mediates angiogenesis and the expression of growth factors in endothelial cells.
source: The PI3K pathway mediates angiogenesis and the expression of growth factors in endothelial cells (Jiang et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2000.

claim: The PI3K pathway regulates Pou3f2 in melanoma cells.
source: The PI3K pathway mediates angiogenesis and the expression of growth factors in endothelial cells (Jiang et al., 2000) and also regulates Pou3f2 in melanoma cells (Bonvin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bonvin et al., 2012.

claim: Pou3f2 promotes neurogenesis.
source: Pou3f2 promotes neurogenesis (Jaegle et al., 2003; Castro et al., 2006; Dominguez et al., 2013; Sugitani et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Pou3f2 activates the Notch ligand Delta1, synergistically with Mash1, to maintain a subset of neural progenitors in an undifferentiated state.
source: Specifically, it activates the Notch ligand Delta1, synergistically with Mash1, to maintain a subset of neural progenitors in an undifferentiated state (Castro et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Castro et al., 2006.

claim: Pou3f2 suppresses the Notch effector Hes5.
source: whereas it suppresses the Notch effector Hes5 (Dominguez et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dominguez et al., 2013.

claim: Hes5 negatively regulates transcription of neurogenesis-promoting genes Neuregulins.
source: whereas it suppresses the Notch effector Hes5 (Dominguez et al., 2013) that negatively regulate transcription of neurogenesis-promoting genes Neuregulins (Imayoshi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Imayoshi et al., 2008.

claim: In human melanoma spheres and tumor xenograft, Pou3f2 is proposed to induce the Notch pathway.
source: In human melanoma spheres and tumor xenograft, Pou3f2 is proposed to induce the Notch pathway (Thurber et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Thurber et al., 2011.

claim: In situ hybridization for Pou3f2 showed that this transcription factor is expressed in most embryo structures, although the staining is particularly evident in the brain region.
source: In situ hybridization for Pou3f2 showed that this transcription factor is expressed in most embryo structures, although the staining is particularly evident in the brain region (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pou3f2 is expressed in both endothelial and hematopoietic cells, although more pronounced in the GFP+ cells from tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 embryos.
source: We found expression of Pou3f2 in both type of cells, although more pronounced in the GFP+ cells from tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR analysis of FACS-purified cells shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Injection of morpholino targeting Pou3f2 resulted in 100% embryo death, as embryo could not reach 50% epiboly stage, at 5.3 hr post-fertilization.
source: Injection of morpholino targeting Pou3f2 (the relevant zebrafish analogue) resulted in 100% embryo death, as embryo could not reach 50% epiboly stage, at 5.3 hr post-fertilization.
evidence: This is based on zebrafish morpholino injection experiments.

claim: When the Pou3f2-targeted morpholino was activated by UV light at six hpf the embryo survival was around 80%.
source: When the Pou3f2-targeted morpholino was activated by UV light at six hpf the embryo survival was around 80%.
evidence: This is based on caged morpholino experiments in zebrafish.

claim: A general phenotype characterized by curved body and curly tail, and specific dysmorphogenesis of the vascular system was observed in most of the tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 embryos following Pou3f2 knockdown.
source: We observed a general phenotype characterized by curved body and curly tail, and specific dysmorphogenesis of the vascular system in most of the tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 embryos (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is demonstrated through imaging of zebrafish embryos shown in Figure 4a.

claim: A reduced number of intersegmental vessels (ISVs) was observed following Pou3f2 knockdown, which could be rescued with Pou3f2 mRNA.
source: A reduced number of intersegmental vessels (ISVs) was observed (Figure 4b–c), which could be rescued with Pou3f2 mRNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated through imaging and quantification shown in Figure 4b-c.

claim: In situ hybridization showed that Fli1 and Kdr were downregulated following Pou3f2 knockdown, particularly evident in the intersegmental vessels.
source: In situ hybridization showed that Fli1 and Kdr were downregulated following Pou3f2 KD, particularly evident in the intersegmental vessels, confirming the role for Pou3f2 in endothelial development (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is demonstrated through in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Fli1 and Kdr were significantly reduced in Pou3f2 knockdown embryos compared to control as confirmed by real-time PCR.
source: These results were confirmed by real-time PCR (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), where Fli1 and Kdr were significantly reduced in Pou3f2 knockdown embryos compared to control.
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Effective knockdown by the morpholino in zebrafish embryos was documented by Western blotting using a Pou3f2-specific antibody.
source: Effective knockdown by the morpholino in zebrafish embryos was documented by Western blotting using a Pou3f2-specific antibody (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is demonstrated through Western blot data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: There was a global reduction of endothelial cells in Pou3f2 knockdown animals, with the percentage of GFP+ cells isolated from the tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 zebrafish embryos at 24 hr post-fertilization being 6.7% of total cells in control compared to 3.7% following Pou3f2 knockdown.
source: In addition, there was a global reduction of endothelial cells in Pou3f2 KD animals. Specifically, the percentage of GFP+ cells isolated from the tg(fli1:EGFP)y1 zebrafish embryos at 24 hr post-fertilization was 6.7% of total cells in control compared to 3.7% following Pou3f2 KD (Figure 4f–g).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FACS analysis shown in Figure 4f-g.

claim: Injection of Pou3f2-targeted caged morpholino in tg(cmyb:GFP) did not significantly reduce the percentage of GFP+ cells, suggesting that Pou3f2 is more critical for endothelial rather than hematopoietic development.
source: Injection of Pou3f2-targeted caged morpholino in tg(cmyb:GFP) did not significantly reduce the percentage of GFP+ cells, suggesting that Pou3f2 is more critical for endothelial rather than hematopoietic development.
evidence: This is based on FACS analysis of hematopoietic cells in zebrafish.

claim: Caged morpholino activation at 24 hpf or later did not produce a significant phenotype, indicating that Pou3f2 is necessary early in endothelial development, but is not required for maintenance of the endothelial phenotype.
source: Notably, caged MO activation at 24 hpf or later did not produce a significant phenotype, indicating that Pou3f2 is necessary early in endothelial development, but is not required for maintenance of the endothelial phenotype.
evidence: This is based on temporal caged morpholino activation experiments in zebrafish.

claim: The lack of expression of Pou3f2 in mature endothelial cells is consistent with the observation that Pou3f2 is necessary early in endothelial development but not required for maintenance.
source: This observation is consistent with the lack of expression of Pou3f2 in mature endothelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the temporal requirement data with expression patterns.

claim: Pou3f2 could act upstream of Notch during endothelial, as well as neuronal development.
source: Our studies suggest that Pou3f2 could act upstream of Notch during endothelial, as well as neuronal development.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental data and known roles of Pou3f2 in neuronal development.

claim: Pou3f2 could have a role in the human vascular diseases caused by mutations in Notch family members, such as Alagille syndrome and cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL).
source: In this regard, Pou3f2 could have a role in the human vascular diseases caused by mutations in Notch family members, such as Alagille syndrome and cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) (Loomes et al., 1999; Joutel et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the potential upstream role of Pou3f2 in Notch signaling, with citations to diseases caused by Notch mutations.

claim: Notch signaling is required for arterio-venous differentiation during vascular development.
source: As Notch signaling is also required for arterio-venous differentiation during vascular development (Lawson et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lawson et al., 2001.

claim: Pou3f2 could be upstream of the eph-ephrin system and play a role in arterio-venous specification.
source: this suggests that Pou3f2 could be also upstream of the eph-ephrin system and play a role in arterio-venous specification.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the role of Notch in arterio-venous differentiation.

claim: Pou3f2 gene expression seems to be controlled by MAPK and Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
source: Pou3f2 gene expression seems to be controlled by MAPK (Goodall et al., 2004b) and Wnt/β-catenin (Goodall et al., 2004a) signaling, two key pathways linked to cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goodall et al., 2004a and 2004b.

claim: Pou3f2 function can be modulated by posttranslational modifications including sumoylation, ubiquitinylation, glycosylation and in particular phosphorylation.
source: Pou3f2 function can be also modulated by posttranslational modifications including sumoylation, ubiquitinylation, glycosylation and in particular phosphorylation (Kasibhatla et al., 1999; Augustijn et al., 2002; Diamond et al., 1999; Nieto et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The expression patterns for Pou3f2 in hiPSC/mEC heterokaryons were similar to that observed in mESC/hEC heterokaryons.
source: To determine the role of Pou3f2 during endothelial differentiation from human iPSC, we examined the expression of Pou3f2 in the heterokaryon system consisting of hiPSCs and murine endothelial cells (Figure 5a). In addition, we examined the expression of Pou3f2 in the hiPSC during our endothelial differentiation protocol (Figure 5b). The expression patterns for Pou3f2 were similar to that which we observed in mESC (Figure 3a and b).
evidence: This is based on comparison of qPCR data from hiPSC and mESC systems shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Accelerated regulation of Pou3f2 was observed in the hiPSCs in the heterokaryon by comparison to hiPSCs exposed to the endothelial differentiation protocol.
source: Notably, we saw the same accelerated regulation of Pou3f2 in the hiPSCs in the heterokaryon by comparison to hiPSCs exposed to the endothelial differentiation protocol.
evidence: This is based on comparison of temporal gene expression patterns.

claim: Pou3f2 shRNA significantly reduced the expression of Pou3f2 during the endothelial differentiation protocol in hiPSCs.
source: Next, we assessed the effects of shRNA-mediated KD of Pou3f2 on differentiation of endothelial cells from human iPSC. Pou3f2 shRNA significantly reduced the expression of Pou3f2 during the endothelial differentiation protocol (Figure 5c,d).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 5c-d.

claim: Pou3f2 knockdown significantly inhibited the expression of endothelial-related genes during the course of the differentiation protocol, including Kdr, Tie2, CDdh5 Pecam1, Nos3 and Vwf.
source: Furthermore, Pou3f2 KD significantly inhibited the expression of endothelial-related genes during the course of the differentiation protocol, including Kdr, Tie2, CDdh5 Pecam1, Nos3 and Vwf (Figure 5e–j).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 5e-j.

claim: Pou3f2 knockdown reduced iPSC-EC generation by ~50%.
source: Notably, Pou3f2 KD also reduced iPSC-EC generation by ~50% (Figure 6a–c).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FACS analysis shown in Figure 6a-c.

claim: Protein expression of CD31, CD144 and Vwf was reduced in ECs derived from Pou3f2 knockdown iPSCs.
source: In addition, protein expression of CD31, CD144 and Vwf (Figure 6d) and formation of tubular networks on matrigel (Figure 6e) were reduced in ECs derived from Pou3f2 KD iPSCs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Formation of tubular networks on matrigel was reduced in ECs derived from Pou3f2 knockdown iPSCs.
source: In addition, protein expression of CD31, CD144 and Vwf (Figure 6d) and formation of tubular networks on matrigel (Figure 6e) were reduced in ECs derived from Pou3f2 KD iPSCs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through matrigel network formation assay shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Pou3f2 knockdown iPSC-ECs exhibited impairment of nitric oxide generation.
source: Furthermore, Pou3f2 KD iPSC-ECs exhibited impairment of other endothelial functions including nitric oxide generation (Figure 6f)
evidence: This is demonstrated through nitric oxide production assay shown in Figure 6f.

claim: Pou3f2 knockdown iPSC-ECs exhibited impairment of uptake of acetylated LDL.
source: Furthermore, Pou3f2 KD iPSC-ECs exhibited impairment of other endothelial functions including nitric oxide generation (Figure 6f), and uptake of acetylated LDL (Figure 6g).
evidence: This is demonstrated through AcLDL uptake assay shown in Figure 6g.

claim: Functional impairments in Pou3f2 knockdown iPSC-ECs were associated with reduced expression of EC markers including Kdr, Tie2, Nos3, CD31, Cdh5 and Vwf.
source: These functional impairments were associated with reduced expression of EC markers including Kdr, Tie2, Nos3, CD31, Cdh5 and Vwf (Figure 6h).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: Endothelial cells derived from iPSCs (hiPSC-ECs) expressed various markers associated with arterial, venous and lymphatic ECs and thereby represent a heterogeneous population of ECs.
source: We have previously shown that endothelial cells derived from iPSCs (hiPSC-ECs) expressed various markers associated with arterial, venous and lymphatic ECs and thereby represent a heterogeneous population of ECs (Rufaihah et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by Rufaihah et al., 2011.

claim: ECs generated from Pou3f2 knockdown iPSCs resemble those generated from wild-type iPSCs with respect to venous (Ephb4 and Coup-TFII) and lymphatic markers (Pdpn and Lyve1) but have a significant reduction of arterial markers (Notch4, Efnb2 and Hey2).
source: We found that ECs generated from Pou3f2 KD iPSCs resemble those generated from wild-type iPSCs with respect to venous (Ephb4 and Coup-TFII) and lymphatic markers (Pdpn and Lyve1) but have a significant reduction of arterial markers (Notch4, Efnb2 and Hey2) compared to scrambled control (Figure 6i).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR analysis of arterial, venous, and lymphatic markers shown in Figure 6i.

claim: During differentiation of iPSCs to ECs, the binding of Pou3f2 to the promoters of endothelial related transcription factors including Ets1, Lmo2, Hey1 and Hey2 was inhibited in Pou3f2 knockdown cells.
source: To determine if Pou3f2 binds to the promoters of endothelial-related transcription factors, we performed ChIP-PCR. We observed that during differentiation of iPSCs to ECs, the binding of Pou3f2 to the promoters of endothelial related transcription factors including Ets1, Lmo2, Hey1 and Hey2 (Figure 7a–d) was inhibited in Pou3f2 KD cells
evidence: This is demonstrated through ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 7a-d.

claim: Reduced binding of Pou3f2 to promoters was associated with reduced gene expression of Ets1, Lmo2, Hey1 and Hey2.
source: We observed that during differentiation of iPSCs to ECs, the binding of Pou3f2 to the promoters of endothelial related transcription factors including Ets1, Lmo2, Hey1 and Hey2 (Figure 7a–d) was inhibited in Pou3f2 KD cells, in association with reduced gene expression of these factors (Figure 7f–i).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 7f-i.

claim: The generation of CD31+CD144+ cells was reduced in the Pou3f2 knockdown hiPSCs and could be rescued with modified mRNA encoding Pou3f2.
source: Finally, we observed that the generation of CD31+CD144+ cells was reduced in the Pou3f2 KD hiPSCs and could be rescued with modified mRNA encoding Pou3f2 (Figure 7j).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FACS analysis with rescue experiments shown in Figure 7j.

claim: Transcription factors and epigenetic machinery which actively maintain endothelial phenotype can also act on the pluripotent cell nucleus to recapitulate ontogeny.
source: Our work suggests that transcription factors and epigenetic machinery which actively maintain endothelial phenotype can also act on the pluripotent cell nucleus to recapitulate ontogeny.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the heterokaryon experiments showing temporal gene expression patterns.
